slides.title: What Safeguarding Means
slides.content: Safeguarding is about: Protecting students from harm. Preventing abuse, exploitation and neglect. Supporting wellbeing and mental health. Making sure concerns can be raised and acted upon. Safeguarding is everyone's responsibility, not just staff responsibility.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'What Safeguarding Means'? Select all that apply.
options: Making sure concerns can be raised and acted upon
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on What Safeguarding Means.

slides.title: College Is Different from School
slides.content: At college: You have more independence. You make more of your own decisions. Staff monitor less directly. You can self-refer for support. Staff still act when there are concerns. You do not need to wait for a teacher to notice a problem.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'College Is Different from School'? Select all that apply.
options: You make more of your own decisions
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on College Is Different from School.

slides.title: What Prevent Is
slides.content: Prevent helps protect people from being drawn into: Radicalisation. Extremism. Terrorism. Extremism includes opposition to fundamental British Values or encouragement of violence against others.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'What Prevent Is'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on What Prevent Is.

slides.title: Vulnerability Factors
slides.content: People may become more vulnerable when they are: Isolated. Looking for belonging. Struggling with identity. Angry or frustrated. Influenced by manipulative online content. Influenced by people encouraging harmful views.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Vulnerability Factors'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Vulnerability Factors.

slides.title: Online Safety Risks
slides.content: Key risks include: Personal Information: Information shared online can be misused. Grooming and Exploitation: People may build trust online for harmful purposes. Financial Scams: Fake jobs, fake offers and "easy money" schemes often target young people. Non-Consensual Images: Sharing intimate or private images without consent is unlawful. Dark Web Risks: The dark web carries significant legal and personal risks.

slides.title: AI and Academic Integrity
slides.content: Do NOT: Submit AI-generated work as your own. Use AI content without acknowledgement. Enter personal or confidential information into public AI tools. Do: Declare AI use when required. Use AI to support learning, not replace learning. Check AI-generated information. Ask your teacher if unsure.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following is a key point about 'AI and Academic Integrity'?
options: Submit AI-generated work as your own
exercise.explanation: This is a key point from the section on AI and Academic Integrity.

slides.title: AI and Data Protection
slides.content: Never enter into public AI systems: Personal details. Student information. Staff details. Confidential college information. If you would not share it publicly, do not enter it into an AI tool.

exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on AI and Data Protection.

slides.title: How ESCG Responds to Concerns
slides.content: The safeguarding process is: 1. A concern is raised. 2. The safeguarding team is informed. 3. The concern is assessed. 4. Appropriate support or action follows. Staff cannot promise complete secrecy if there is a risk of harm.

exercise.prompt: What is a key message of 'How ESCG Responds to Concerns'?

It is optional and not required

slides.title: How to Report Concerns
slides.content: If worried about yourself or someone else: Tell a trusted member of staff. Contact the safeguarding team. Contact the wellbeing team. Report anonymously if needed. You do not need proof to report a concern.
